tool_input.command: cat node_modules/@guren/server/dist/http/middleware/rate-limit.d.ts; F=$(grep -l "function createApiToken" node_modules/@guren/server/dist/*.js); echo $F; grep -n "function createApiToken\|function verifyApiToken\|function parseApiToken\|function createBearerTokenMiddleware\|hashToken\|function hash" $F | head
tool_input.description: Read rate limit declarations and token impl location

result:
Personal API tokens are working. `bun run typecheck` passes, `bun test` passes (8 tests, including 6 new ones for this feature), and `bunx guren gate` passes all six CI stages. I didn't start the app or test it over real HTTP; the tests run requests in-process.

- **Storage:** tokens look like `<public id>|<64-char random secret>`. The new `api_tokens` table keeps the public id, the name, the owner and a SHA-256 hash of the secret, never the secret itself. The token is returned only once, in the create response.
- **Creating and revoking:** `POST /profile/tokens` and `DELETE /profile/tokens/:id` behave as the contract says (201, 204, 422, 404). Both require a signed-in session. The profile page now lists the user's tokens by name and has a create form (which shows the new token once) and Revoke buttons.
- **Posts API:** `GET /api/posts` returns every post, newest first. `POST /api/posts` always sets the author to the token's owner, even if the body sends an `authorId`. It uses the same validation as the web form. A missing, bad or revoked token gets a JSON 401 before anything else runs.
- **Rate limit:** the limit is counted per token id, so each of a user's tokens gets its own 60 per minute. The 61st request gets a 429 with `Retry-After`.

**Limitation:** the rate-limit counts live in the server process's memory. If the site runs on more than one server, each one counts separately, so a script could get more than 60 a minute in total. Restarting the server also resets the counts. A shared store such as Redis would fix that.

I built this on the framework's own API-token and rate-limit tools rather than writing new ones. The new table is in `db/schema.ts`, with a migration in `db/migrations/20260925030142_create_api_tokens/`, and there's a read-only `ApiToken` model in `app/Models/ApiToken.ts`. The token store and the two API middlewares are in `app/Auth/apiTokens.ts`. Controllers are `app/Http/Controllers/ApiTokenController.ts` and `app/Http/Controllers/Api/ApiPostController.ts`. The API controller has its own name because the audit stage rejects two classes called `PostController`. The token name rules are in `app/Http/Validators/ApiTokenValidator.ts`. The API routes are in a new `routes/api.ts`, mounted from `routes/web.ts`, and the token routes were added to `routes/auth.ts`. `ProfileController` and `resources/js/pages/profile/Edit.tsx` were changed for the token list, and the new tests are in `tests/controllers/ApiTokenController.test.ts`.
